hook: China's great teacher, whose ideas on family and good government shaped East Asia.

pages.x: Kong Qiu was born in 551 BC in the small state of Lu, in eastern China. His father, an old soldier, died when he was three, and he grew up poor, keeping granaries and stables while teaching himself history, poetry, music and ceremony. He became Kong Fuzi, "Master Kong", which Europeans turned into Confucius.

Around the age of 30 he began to teach, and took any student who could bring even a bundle of dried meat as a fee, rich or poor. He is said to have had 3,000 students. Anyone, he taught, could become a true gentleman through learning and good conduct, not only those born noble.

He loved music above almost anything. After hearing an ancient piece called the Shao, his students wrote, he did not notice the taste of meat for three months. "I never imagined music could reach such heights," he said.

He became a minister in Lu, but left in disgust when its duke spent his days watching dancing girls sent by a rival. For 14 years he wandered from state to state looking for a ruler who would put his ideas to work. None did, and once his group was surrounded and nearly starved.

After his death his students gathered his sayings in the Analects. "What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others." "Is it not a joy to learn, and to practise what you have learned?" He taught respect for parents, honesty, loyalty, and ruling by good example instead of punishment.

Three centuries after his death, the Han emperors made his teachings China's official philosophy. For 2,000 years, until 1905, anyone who wanted to be a government official had to pass exams on the Confucian classics.

Confucius shaped the values of China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam more than anyone: respect for family, love of learning, and duty in government. His family tree is the longest ever recorded, with more than 80 generations.
pts: Taught a Golden Rule 500 years before Jesus
His ideas guided Chinese government for 2,000 years
